title: A rule
goal: A directive you say becomes one rule with a tag and a scope, kept only on your stamp, shown to every agent, read against every page, and enforced: a build that breaks it goes back to be rewritten and never goes live.
lead: A rule. You say a directive; Identity restates it as one rule with a tag (always, ask, refuse, goal) and a scope and asks; on your stamp the rule is on the record and every agent's card shows it; Check reads every page against it; a build that breaks it is sent back, twice at most, and then you are told.
ends_when: The rule is on the record and enforced by the line, or you refused it and nothing was kept.

steps.text: You say a directive ("never say X", "always show the phone number").
Identity restates it as one rule with a tag (always / ask / refuse / goal) and a scope, and asks: "A rule, as understood: …".

steps.short: You stamp; it is on the record
steps.text: You stamp. The rule is written on the record with its id, tag, line and your words; the Brief gets "A rule, from now on: …".
Every agent step's card shows the rules; Identity's take reads them as THE RULES.
Check lists the rules that apply to the pages and reads each page against them; a broken rule files the Build failed with the finding.
The line sends the build back to Write with the finding, twice at most; then you are told.

edges.trigger: The rule is already on the record.
edges.code_does: identity_file (a directive, or a rule the take read out of a task) says the department already has the rule and files nothing; _rule_answered does the same for an answered rule ask.

outcome.golden: the department already has this rule

site.text: It replaces the goal and the next publish asks again (publish_asks_from).

edges.code_does: identity_apply replaces the goal, keeps goals[], bumps identity_revision and re-arms the first-publish ask. The cycle is not reopened (J2.8).
identity_drop keeps nothing; a refused rule that answered Identity's own question asks the question again.

edges.short: A child's rule is looser than Root's
edges.trigger: A child's rule is looser than Root's.

site.text: Identity's own check at birth keeps the child's rules within the parent's (a born Root rule).

edges.code_does: A rule that matches an inherited ask or refuse rule with a looser tag is not asked for and not written; matching is by normalised line. _rule_ask checks the rule against the rules the ancestors hold (_effective_rules less the department's own, through rule_faults) before it files the ask, so the owner is never asked to stamp a rule that would be turned down; identity_apply checks again before it writes, since an ancestor's rule may change between the ask and the stamp. Either way Identity says "Root's rule stands: a department's rules can only tighten it" and a row on the record says so. A prohibition tagged always counts as refuse; a positive always rule and a goal are not compared (BL-2b).

outcome.golden: a department's rules can only tighten it

edges.reword: A department's rules can only tighten Root's. Built for a rule an ancestor stamped: the same line with a looser tag is not asked for and not kept. A looser rule worded differently is not caught yet.

edges.short: A rule the take reads out of a task
edges.trigger: A rule the take reads out of a task.

site.text: Asked as a rule before the task is filed (J3.3).

edges.code_does: The same as J3.3: identity_file asks for the rule first (_rule_ask), then files the task.

edges.trigger: The build still breaks the rule after two returns.

site.text: You are told; the build stays failed; nothing publishes (_send_back).

edges.code_does: _send_back stops at two returns and tells the owner ("two rewrites did not mend it. Say the rule another way, or drop it."), then files one ask through _blocked with the ways out (say the rule another way, leave this rule out, stop); the build stays failed and nothing goes live until the owner chooses, and leaving the rule out takes it off the department's rules (leave_rule_out) so the line builds again without it. The end is never a tell only.

outcome.golden: two rewrites did not mend it

rulings.text: Approval settings live per department, inherited from Root; a department may only tighten.
Authority: the AI has the whole authority to make things happen unless a person says something; no ask stops a run by default; a person narrows with a rule, a Stop, a refusal.

scenarios.says: A directive becomes a rule on the owner's stamp, reaches every card, is read against every page, and a build that breaks it is sent back twice and never goes live, with a stubbed model.

backlog.smallest: Rules that differ in wording but not in meaning, and a positive always rule against a go rule, are not compared: matching is by normalised line, and Root's own born rules are always and go, so today the check reaches a rule an ancestor stamped. A stricter law (a model reading of looseness) is a later amendment.
